posts.text: I just got my first ever hackathon podium, and it happened at Hack the North, Canada’s largest hackathon! We won 2nd place in the GPTZero sponsor track with Snitch! Still trying to soak it in. I signed up for Hack the North to get back into hackathons, build something fun, meet interesting people, and experience more of the North American tech scene. I’ve lived in Singapore all my life, a place I’ve always loved and felt very comfortable in. But growth doesn’t happen in comfort zones. That’s why I’ll be spending the next year in Toronto, Canada as part of the NUS Overseas Colleges programme, where I’ll be working as a Software Engineer Intern at trax.co 🇨🇦. So far, Toronto has been great: welcoming people, beautiful walks, and a refreshing change of pace. Excited to learn, build, and see what the year ahead holds! #NewBeginnings #Toronto #So

Just last month, I finished my first internship at Perfingo, and it was an eye-opening, humbling, and genuinely exciting experience. It came with a lot of firsts: - Writing code that actually made it to production, not just localhost - Building real features used by real users - Working with AWS for authentication and databases - Developing a production iOS app with Flutter - And most importantly, working on something not graded, but shipped Of course, it wasn’t smooth sailing. One fun part about working at a startup is that you end up wearing many hats. For me, as a usually-introverted SWE intern, that meant stepping out of my comfort zone. A couple of weeks ago, I helped represent Perfingo at the SOC Startup Recruitment Fair and the Block71 SEC Startup Shuffle, pitching our company to prospective interns and people curious about the startup scene.
